116 of Table 1’s 120 fields come back as printed, and all 180 of Table 2 and S1 Table 1, which adds pathway models B and C. The four others are slips in the paper. Scenario 1’s MH3,1 has ℓ = 9,910.49, which rounds to 0.9910 × 10⁴, not the printed 0.9911. In scenario 2 the paper ranks MH1,1, MH1,2 and MH1,3 12, 10 and 11, but its own BICs for them, −13.831, −13.768 and −13.766, put them 10, 11 and 12. Refitted from scratch, the 24 models give the same table, slips and all.

What came back

The likelihood in Python
odemm.py reads each model (rates, mean or median constraint, noise parameters, weights) from the authors’ fitting script and evaluates logLikelihood.m. At the 51 saved optima it gives the saved log-likelihood to within 9 × 10⁻⁴. The conversion reaction is solved in closed form, where the authors used CVODES.
Every panel, as the scripts plot it
MATLAB’s hist with bin centres, the staircase fills, pchip interpolation of the noise parameters and intervals from getConfidenceIntervals.m, all from the optima, Hessians and profile likelihoods the authors saved in Code S1.
Table 1, refitted
All 24 conversion-reaction models, fitted again from scratch: 2,000 Latin hypercube starts each inside the authors’ bounds, L-BFGS-B with exact gradients from JAX. Every one reaches the saved optimum (within 9 × 10⁻⁴ in ℓ); the best value is found by 12 to 1,865 of the starts.
The saved optima hold
For 49 of the 51 saved optima the exact gradient was computed, and a local L-BFGS-B run started there gains at most 6 × 10⁻⁵ in ℓ. The JAX solver fails at the other two; the numpy port reproduces their ℓ.
Fig. 6’s early stop
From a random start, EM stopped by MATLAB’s rule ends at 68.0 / 32.0% in 289 of 300 starts. Run to convergence it gives 68.1 / 31.9%, so the published weights carry MATLAB’s stopping rule.
A mislabelled time point
The kinetic data file labels its second time point “10 min”. The scripts and the paper use 5 min, and so do we.

What stayed buried

  • The fit behind Fig. 5C’s 71.5% for pathway model B. Its saved MH3,3 gives 69.8%
  • The 500 random cells behind the dashed means of Fig. 2E, and the sample trajectories drawn in Figs 2B and 2E
  • A blind refit of the NGF models. At the authors’ start counts, L-BFGS-B does not reach the saved optima of pathway model A (ℓ = −43,278 against −40,348 for MH2,1): about half the starts fail in the ODE solve at the extreme rates the bounds allow

Figs 2 to 6 and the three tables come back from the authors’ saved fits. One pie in Fig. 5C does not.

What we matched

The figures are MATLAB plots, and PLOS keeps the original 600 dpi files. Inside each axes box we erased the published figure and drew our panel there, from the authors’ saved fits. Axes, labels, legends and schematics outside the boxes are the paper’s; nothing inside a box is fitted to it.

Our run
Code S1, the authors’ MATLAB implementation with its data and every saved fit, ported to Python. Each panel is computed as the authors’ plotting scripts compute it, from the saved optima, Hessians and profile likelihoods.
Axes
Each axes box is snapped to the published box lines, and data map to pixels linearly or on log10 between the axis limits the plotting scripts set.
Lines and colours
MATLAB’s line widths at the figure’s scale, and MATLAB’s colours as the publisher’s CMYK conversion printed them. Histograms, fills and interval bars keep MATLAB’s black edges.
Scores
For each colour, the share of published pixels within 4 px of ours, and of ours within 4 px of the published ones. Each figure lists, per panel, the lowest share each way over the axes and colours the pipeline checks; report.md has every one. Legends and labels inside a box are left out.
Reading the views
Overlay: ink is the paper only, light green is the reproduction only, dark green is both. Difference: darker means a larger grey-level difference (×2). Most text inside a box is erased with the figure, so it shows as the paper’s only.
Images
Both images are scaled down from the 600 dpi files for this page and share one 256-colour palette; the scores come from the full-size files.

We rebuild this page each time the pipeline runs.
